One day you are setting up workplaces and accounts for four new starters; the next you are on the phone with our network supplier about a switch in the warehouse, or sorting out a DNS record for a new domain. Every other team depends on us, and you report to the Team Lead of Essentials. Your role as System Engineer Workplaces. You manage our laptops, phones, screens and peripherals end to end — deployment, software, updates and support. Colleagues come to you when something doesn’t work, and you make sure it does. Onboarding and offboarding. You arrange accounts, licences, access rights and hardware so new colleagues can start properly, and you close everything down cleanly and securely when someone leaves. You also look for ways to automate this instead of doing it by hand every time. Cloud workplace and identity. You manage our cloud identity, mail and collaboration environment: accounts and groups, mailboxes and shared mailboxes, multi-factor authentication, access policies and licences. Network. You keep the network running across our sites — WiFi, switches, firewall, VPN and the connections between Dordrecht, Alblasserdam and Herentals. Straightforward work you handle yourself; for the bigger pieces you steer our suppliers. Suppliers and contracts. You are our contact person for hardware suppliers, internet providers and service partners. You escalate, chase tickets, hold them to their SLA, keep an eye on renewals and costs, and order what we need. Domains, DNS and certificates. You manage our domain registrations, DNS records, SSL certificates and mail authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC). Security and compliance. You keep endpoint protection, backups and access policies in order, pick up security alerts, maintain our asset register, and support our ISO 27001 and NIS2 work. Documentation and improvement. You write things down so the next person can follow them, and you pick up improvement projects: rollouts, migrations and automation. This is you MBO-4 or HBO in ICT, and 2 to 5 years’ experience in a broad system administration, workplace management or IT support role. You are at home in a Microsoft cloud workplace — identity, mail, collaboration — and you have worked with modern endpoint management to roll out and secure devices centrally. You have solid networking fundamentals: VLANs, DHCP, DNS, WiFi and firewall rules. You can read a network diagram and follow a problem through it. You are comfortable managing suppliers: you ask the next question, don’t let a ticket go quiet, and know when to escalate. Certification such as MD-102, MS-102, AZ-104, CCNA or a firewall vendor equivalent is a plus. So is scripting — if you’d rather automate a task than repeat it, we’ll like you.
